data.title: Nosice – Hradisko, a Púchov culture hillfort and Slavic graves by the dam
data.excerpt: During the construction of the Nosice dam, three Slavic inhumation graves of the 9th century came to light – the only form of burial of the Slavic population known from the whole of northern Slovakia. Nearby lies the locality of Hradisko, an enclosure of 80 × 40 m girdled by two earthen ramparts, dated by pottery to the end of the 1st century BC and built by the people of the Púchov culture for their own protection.
data.metaTitle: Nosice – Hradisko and a Great Moravian cemetery
data.metaDescription: During the construction of the Nosice dam, three Slavic inhumation graves of the 9th century were found — a rare record of Great Moravian burial in the north.

children.text: During the construction of the Nosice dam, three Slavic inhumation graves laid shallowly beneath the surface were also found, which date from the 9th century. Prof. V. Budinský-Krička assumed that there was a flat inhumation cemetery of Great Moravian date here. It cannot be ruled out, however, that the graves may originally have been covered by burial mounds. From the whole territory of northern Slovakia this is the only form of burial of the Slavic population that we know. We may therefore assume that the original burial mounds may already have been lowered to such an extent that they could no longer be identified in the field.

Ernest Poliak from Púchov identified a settlement of the Púchov culture on the slope of the hillfort, and another one between the Váh canal and the railway line. Rim sections of large storage jars were also found here, in which the people of the Púchov culture stored their supplies of food.

Close to the village there is also the locality of Hradisko. It belongs, admittedly, to the cadastral area of Púchov, but since it is much closer to Nosice, we list it among the find spots of this village. Pottery dates the fortification to the end of the 1st century BC. The protected area measures 80 × 40 m and is girdled by two earthen ramparts. The entrance to the fortification is placed on the northern side, and roughly halfway along the length of the southern rampart there is a cistern (?) – a pit for collecting rainwater. Besides pottery, a stone quern for grinding grain was also found here. Below the slope of the fortification E. Poliak also identified a settlement of the Púchov culture, whose inhabitants evidently built this fortlet for their own protection. The repeated occurrence of settlement-plus-fortification pairs is already the rule in this period. It evidently arose from the expected invasion of the Germanic peoples, which took place precisely just at the beginning of the 1st century AD and affected the whole territory of northern Slovakia.

children.text: In 2000 a field survey led by Jozef Moravčík was carried out at the hillfort, during which several interesting finds of the period of the Púchov culture were made. The most interesting among them is an iron socketed axe, typical of the Púchov culture.

Text taken from: Martin Olšovský, Štefan Meliš, Jozef Moravčík: Po stopách predkov, Archeológia Stredného Považia od praveku po stredovek – súbor dokumentov a fotografií, published at his own expense by Martin Olšovský in 2008 in an edition of 4 copies.
